item.title: Liverpool manager knows how Arsenal stars work as he plots their downfall
item.description: Liverpool manager knows how Arsenal stars work as he plots their downfall Andoni Iraola may have only taken charge of Liverpool this season, but he is no stranger to facing Arsenal. The Spaniard previously managed Bournemouth for several years and came up against the Gunners on multiple occasions during his time at the club. He has proved to be a difficult opponent for Mikel Arteta in recent meetings, having guided Bournemouth to some impressive performances against Arsenal. Those experiences mean Iraola already understands the challenge posed by the Gunners. However, Sunday’s fixture will be his first meeting with Arsenal as Liverpool manager. His team will enter the game on a five-match winning run, giving them momentum as they prepare for one of their biggest tests of the season. Iraola has faced many Premier League opponents during his time in English football, and Arsenal are among the teams he knows particularly well. That familiarity should help him prepare his players for what should be a demanding encounter. Iraola knows the challenge Arsenal pose Arsenal have been among the strongest teams in the league over recent seasons and are the defending champions . Their quality, organisation and consistency make them formidable opponents, and Liverpool will need to be at their best to secure a positive result. Expectations are high at Anfield whenever Arsenal visit, and Iraola appears fully aware of the task awaiting his side. He has recognised the quality of Arteta’s players and the understanding they have developed through playing together. The Liverpool boss also believes his own squad has the ability to compete, particularly with the support of the home crowd behind them. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Liverpool manager backs his players Speaking via the Liverpool website , Iraola explained what makes Arsenal such a difficult opponent while expressing confidence in his own team ahead of Sunday’s match. “We know Arsenal, we know how good they are, very good players, working a lot, working in synchrony, knowing each other very well and we have to be ready for that challenge. I think it’s going to be demanding, the game, but I also trust our players, trust ourselves and in a good atmosphere that for sure we will have on Sunday, I hope we can be at the level to win this game.” _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Napoli star confirmed to miss Juventus match
item.description: Napoli star confirmed to miss Juventus match Juventus have received a boost ahead of their meeting with Napoli this weekend , with one of the visitors’ most reliable players set to miss the fixture through injury. Stanislav Lobotka will be unavailable, giving the Bianconeri a potential advantage before a match they regard as particularly important. The Old Lady see the contest as a must win. victory would send a strong message to the rest of the league and lift the team’s confidence, while dropping points could leave them in a difficult position. Juventus know the pressure that comes with being one of the biggest clubs in world football. They do not want their struggles to continue, and this weekend offers an opportunity to show they are ready to compete. Lobotka absence changes Napoli’s options Napoli performed well in their previous match, but they will face Juventus without Lobotka. The midfielder is an important figure in their team, making his absence a significant setback. La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Lobotka is expected to miss several matches in the coming weeks after being stretchered off during Napoli’s previous game. His injury means he will not be available against Juventus, leaving the visitors without one of their dependable performers. His absence could affect Napoli’s plans. Juventus will recognise the opportunity, but must still approach the contest with care. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Juventus must remain alert against Napoli Although Napoli will be without Lobotka, they still have several dangerous players capable of causing problems for Juventus. The home side cannot assume his absence will make the match straightforward, and they will need to remain focused. For Juventus, the priority will be to make the most of this boost while respecting the quality Napoli still possess. A win would provide the response the Old Lady are looking for and strengthen their confidence, while anything less could increase the pressure. Despite Napoli’s setback, Juventus know they must earn the result on the pitch. The Bianconeri will need a strong performance to secure the victory they believe they need.

item.title: “Got to be off” – Chelsea player having a “shocker” can’t continue say journalists
item.description: “Got to be off” – Chelsea player having a “shocker” can’t continue say journalists Chelsea are playing a low quality but high entertainment game against Man U, and one player in particular is struggling. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Chelsea and Manchester United have reached half time at 0-0 in a strange but entertaining game at Stamford Bridge. Both teams have made lots of defensive mistakes, and it’s a very open affair. Both teams have also had their moments in attack. But they are both making it clear what they are – very flawed teams. Chelsea have their excuses for their issues – don’t forget they’re without their first choice goalkeeper, striker, their captain and two best left backs. But those players on the pitch are good enough to do far better. Chelsea fans and journalists call out Fofana shocker Xabi Alonso on the touchline. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) One person getting the worst of the criticism is Wesley Fofana, who has continued to frustrated Chelsea fans pretty much since he arrived at the club. “Welsey Fofana is having a shocker,” said Kieran Gill of the Daily Mail. “He’s got to be off at half time” said influencer Charlie Patrick. “Good god Wesley Fofana” said Lloyd Canfield of the Sun. “Sub off Wesley Fofana,” said internet pundit CFCCentral. To be fair to him, half the time he’s been put in these bad positions by his teammates. Marco Palestra has left him high and dry a couple of times. But Fofana has taken those situations and made them worse. In other news… We said we would get some answers abut certain players in this game – and we certainly have. We’re not sure we like what we’ve found out. Two Chelsea players who are starting today have been named as potential Ballon d’Or winners of the future on TNT Sport.

item.title: 'Un-Australian' - Warner tears into former side after SA charge to win
item.description: Kagiso Rabada took three wickets in the first half an hour to put South Africa on their way to victory [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day five of five) South Africa 329 & 387: Mulder 115, Rickelton 101 Australia 429 & 111: Lyon 33*; Rabada 3-39; Harmer 6-16 South Africa won by 176 runs Scorecard David Warner labelled Australia "terrible", "utterly disgraceful" and "un-Australian" as his former side crumbled under the pressure of a final-day chase and allowed South Africa to charge to a famous Test and series victory in Cape Town. Chasing 288 to win an enthralling contest themselves, Australia lost two wickets in the first over bowled by Kagiso Rabada and never recovered. Rabada was irresistible, also adding the key wicket of Travis Head caught at slip in a superb first spell to become the fastest bowler to 350 Test wickets. But Australia played a part in their own downfall, with Josh Inglis run out for four after inexplicably being called through by Cameron Green. That opened the door to spinner Simon Harmer, who had Alex Carey caught reverse sweeping with just two to his name and Cooper Connolly caught behind for a two-ball duck. At 60-7 at lunch, former opener Warner, who retired from Test cricket in January 2024, tore into his former team-mates. "It is terrible," he said on Fox Sports. "It is un-Australian. There is no fight whatsoever. It is disgraceful. "The batters have let the bowlers down all series. [Matt] Renshaw showed fight in that first Test but I think the batters have been utterly disgraceful." Defeat comes at the start of an intense run of Test cricket for Pat Cummins' side, with attention now turning to four Tests at home against New Zealand starting in December before a five-Test tour of India, the 150th anniversary Test against England in March and next summer's Ashes. The consequences could be significant. South Africa's fine victory, earned across three fascinatingly fluctuating Tests, means the Proteas regain their position at the top of the world rankings and reaffirms their status as one of the world's very best sides. item.title: Colts Ready to Talk About Jonathan Taylor Trade; Vikings in the Mix
item.description: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The undefeated Minnesota Vikings are in Detroit Sunday looking to move to 7-0 on the season and 3-0 in the NFC North against the Lions. Running back Aaron Jones was a full participant Friday and did not receive a game designation, but we know he’s been dealing with an MCL injury all season . That hasn’t held the Vikings back from leaning on him while Jordan Mason was on the injured list for four weeks. Through six games, Jones has rushed 105 times for 436 yards (4.2 per carry). That’s nearly as many carries (132) as he took in 12 games last season. Jordan Mason played Week 1, then came off injured reserve Oct. 24 and led the team with 15 carries for 68 yards against Indianapolis in Week 7, off the Vikings bye. In two games, Mason has 30 carries for 127 yards. So, the Minnesota Vikings’ backfield is as healthy as it has been all season. However, with questions surrounding Jones’ knee, and the team’s lack of efficiency on the ground early this season have general manager Nolan Teasley in the market for a running back before the trade deadline on Nov. 10. Indianapolis Colts now open to trading Jonathan Taylor Meanwhile, the Indianapolis Colts fell to 2-5 on the season with their loss to the Vikings in Week 7. Then on Tuesday, they traded Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. At the time, they were not as interested in trading their one and only offensive superstar, running back Jonathan Taylor. As of Saturday morning, though, they seem to be changing that tune. According to Adam Schefter (ESPN) , the Colts are now open dealing Taylor at some point over the next 10 days. The Indianapolis Colts now are open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told @RapSheet and me. item.title: Pirates Top Prospects No. 1: Seth Hernandez a Future Ace
item.description: This is one in a series of stories breaking down PBN’s Top 30 Pirates prospects . If a team could make an amateur pitcher in a lab to give them exactly what they want, he would probably look like Seth Hernandez. The Pirates selected the right-hander out of high school in California with the sixth pick in the 2025 draft. The 6-4, 190-pound Hernandez has the build. He has the pitches — a fastball capable of touching triple digits, a plus-curveball, a changeup that already showed promise and is improving, and a slider as a fourth offering. He’s also athletic for a pitcher, has a repeatable delivery, high confidence and a strong work ethic. Now, Hernandez has the performance to back the upside. The 20-year-old made his professional debut this year. He began started the season with Low-A Bradenton and won the Florida State League Pitcher of the Month for April. In six starts with the Marauders, Hernandez went 3-0 with a 0.96 ERA. He struck out 50 batters in 28 innings and limited opponents to a .135 batting average. The Pirates quickly promoted Hernandez to High-A Greensboro on May 12. In the hitter-friendly South Atlantic League, he continued to perform. Hernandez made a dozen starts as a Grasshopper and went 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA. He logged 46 innings, walked 24 and struck out 68. Opponents hit .209 against him. Unfortunately for Hernandez, an oblique injury in July ended his season. His stint on the IL lasted the rest of the season, but Hernandez is feeling 100% healthy, he recently said in a Zoom interview after being named Pittsburgh’s minor-league pitcher of the year. Hernandez also represented the Pirates at this year’s Futures games along with outfield prospect Edward Florentino. Hernandez struck out two and needed 14 pitches to complete a perfect second inning in that contest. The Pirates have done well developing starting pitching in recent years. Paul Skenes, Braxton Ashcraft, Jared Jones and Bubba Chandler were all drafted by the Pirates and have made their respective debuts in the last three years. All four were a big part of Pittsburgh’s rotation this year and will be moving forward. Hernandez looks poised to join them in relatively short order. In fact, the 2025 first-rounder said his goal is to make it to the big leagues in 2027. It’s an aggressive goal, and one that could be hard to accomplish next season. But with how quickly Hernandez got acclimated to professional baseball, he could continue to rise quickly through the organization. Regardless of when he arrives in Pittsburgh, Hernandez could one day give the Pirates an ace atop their rotation. All four were a big part of Pittsburgh’s rotation this year and will be moving forward. Hernandez looks poised to join them in relatively short order. In fact, the 2025 first-rounder said his goal is to make it to the big leagues in 2027. It’s an aggressive goal, and one that could be hard to accomplish next season. But with how quickly Hernandez got acclimated to professional baseball, he could continue to rise quickly through the organization. Regardless of when he arrives in Pittsburgh, Hernandez could one day give the Pirates an ace atop their rotation. The 18-year-old has developed into one of the most highly regarded young attackers in European football, and the possibility of a move for around £50m has understandably caught attention across the market. The background here matters. Liverpool’s recruitment in recent windows has shown a clear willingness to invest heavily in elite-level quality and high-end potential. That approach has already delivered major arrivals, with the club prioritising players capable of shaping the next cycle of the squad under Andoni Iraola. item.title: Araujo convinced Liverpool have another gear ahead of hosting Arsenal
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Liverpool's Ronald Araujo (R) celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield. (is associated with: «Araujo convinced Liverpool have another gear ahead of hosting Arsenal») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Ronald Araujo believes there is still much more to come from Liverpool as they bid to extend their winning run to six consecutive games when Arsenal visit Anfield on Sunday. Andoni Iraola’s side can move to within three points of the champions with a victory, having put behind them a stuttering start to the season in which they drew three of their opening four Premier League matches. Since a 3-0 defeat at home to Manchester City after the international window, Liverpool having recorded high-scoring Champions League wins over LASK and Villarreal, Premier League victories over Brentford and Brighton, and a penalty shoot-out success over Chelsea in the League Cup. Sunday will be their fourth straight home game and an opportunity to keep that strong run going. “There’s no doubt we’re in a good moment,” defender Araujo said on the club’s website. “Personally, I’m convinced about the team that we have. “Perhaps we didn’t get the best of starts but, given the team that we have and the work and the philosophy the manager has for us, I was convinced that the team would continue to grow. We’re in that development phase and it’s great because that means that there is still room for improvement. “Now we have a really big challenge in front of us this weekend against a big rival, but we’re playing at home with our fans and we’ll give everything to get that victory.” Arsenal make the trip back north just a few days after a humbling penalty shoot-out loss to fourth-tier Fleetwood, dumping them out of the League Cup. Iraola enjoyed wins over Arsenal in three of his last four meetings while in charge of Bournemouth, but the Spaniard said that record would be irrelevant this weekend. “It’s true that we had good results with Bournemouth against them, but this doesn’t mean a lot, honestly,” Iraola said. “It’s a totally different team, different group of players, different moments so I think we cannot use exactly the same things we used with Bournemouth against Arsenal.” And Iraola can certainly no longer play the underdog card with the Anfield crowd behind him and his players. “I knew since the first day I stepped into this building, I knew this was going to happen – it doesn’t matter the position, it doesn’t matter the competition,” he said. “We accept this. It is always a good thing also in the people expecting a lot of things from your team. “It doesn’t change a lot the approach of the game. At the end it’s a matter of how can we have more chances than the opposition, more chances the Arsenal. We know they are very good defensively.”

item.title: Confirmed: Chatzialexiou to succeed Krösche as Eintracht Frankfurt's board member for sport
item.description: Confirmed: Chatzialexiou to succeed Krösche as Eintracht Frankfurt's board member for sport Following Markus Krösche's departure as board member for sport earlier this month, Eintracht Frankfurt have now found his successor. Die Adler announced on Saturday that Joti Chatzialexiou, currently managing director for sport at 1. FC Nürnberg, will take up the position on February 1 after a release clause in his contract with the 2. Bundesliga club has been triggered. “Joti Chatzialexiou is a proven expert who I have known and respected for many years. He has an outstanding network, extensive experience in developing sporting structures, and a clear understanding of the demands of modern professional football," said Eintracht Frankfurt CEO Axel Hellmann. "Our task is to align Eintracht Frankfurt’s sporting ambitions with financial stability and the sustainable development of the entire club. To that end, a tight and trusting bond among the entire executive board is of vital importance – and Joti will play a key role in that. "We wholeheartedly respect the fact that Joti still has a job at 1. FC Nürnberg, and we really admire the work he has done there. We’re all the more pleased that, when he takes up his role here on 1 February 2027, we’ll be able to shape the next chapter of our development together.”

For the Tigers and Dodgers in 2026, Skubal had a 2.72 ERA (2.51 FIP) and 0.96 WHIP while fanning 186 batters in 158.2 innings over 26 starts. Skubal's arsenal is electric, with him primarily featuring a four-seam fastball that averaged 96.8 mph this past season, as well as a dominant changeup, sinker, and slider. In 2026, Skubal's stuff unsurprisingly rated near the top of the league , with his overall pitching run value in the 97th percentile. Meanwhile, his vaunted changeup had an absurd whiff percentage of 46.9. Starting pitchers Michael King and Clay Holmes could be pricey in terms of average annual value, but won't get the kind of lengthy deal Skubal could command. Teruaki Sato , who is being posted by his Japanese club, could get a relatively big deal. Also off the books will be the $6 million the club is still paying Luke Weaver for 2027 following his trade to the Pirates. Then, ahead of the 2029 season, the Mets have roughly $90 million set to come off, reducing their overall obligations to around $106 million. Given the coming payroll relief and the influx of young, relatively inexpensive players (including McLean, Scott, Carson Benge , A.J. Ewing , and Zac Thornton ), the Mets are in strong position to absorb the kind of massive payroll obligation Skubal's contract will be. There's also the fact that David Stearns seems to be in a make-or-break offseason, and could certainly use a bold and potentially tenure-defining move over the next few months -- even if it might come with some prodding from owner Steve Cohen . Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) throws a pitch in the first inning of the MLB National League game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Los Angeles Dodgers at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati on Monday, Sept. 14, 2026. / USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect CONS The biggest concern when it comes to a megadeal for Skubal or any other pitcher revolves around health. Skubal's 2026 campaign was briefly interrupted by NanoScope surgery on his pitching elbow that kept him out of action from April 30 through June 13. But he continued to be dominant upon his return. After having a 2.70 ERA (2.11 FIP) over his first seven starts, Skubal had a 2.73 ERA (2.66 FIP) in the 19 starts he made post-surgery, with 10 of them coming after he was dealt to the Dodgers at the trade deadline. While Skubal seems to be out of the woods, he has had serious elbow issues in the past. Skubal had Tommy John surgery while in college in 2017 and underwent flexor tendon surgery in August of 2022. One example was at tight end, where through six games, Jake Ferguson played 275 offensive snaps to Brevyn Spann-Ford’s 149. Against Philadelphia they were separated by only two snaps, 36 for Spann-Ford to 38 for Ferguson. That's the type of change needed and the top storyline coming out of Week 7. Coaching staff made adjustments to who gets to play The Spann-Ford and Ferguson adjustment wasn’t the only change. Schottenheimer also benched George Pickens for run plays. item.description: MaxPreps, what are you going to do now? Week 11 saw three teams currently in the Open Division teams lose by double digits. Lakeland dominated The First Academy 35-0. Okay, so there are two ways of looking at this. One is the MaxPreps computer way, the other is the human way. The MaxPreps rankings alone will determine the Open Division. item.title: Scouting Notes: Michigan commit scores five times in Kenowa Hills' win over GR Christian
item.description: Grand Rapids (Mich.) Kenowa Hills is one of the favorites to make a deeper run in Michigan’s Division 4. The Knights had to withstand a push from a pesky Grand Rapids Christian who came in at 4-5. The game was tied at 21 at one point but Kenowa took control and stretched their lead out en route to a 49-35 victory. Kenowa was led by Michigan commit Lundon Hampton , who scored five touchdowns — four rushing, one receiving. Hampton is a bigger back at 6-foot-2, 195 pounds. He is an angular runner, a slasher who has some short-area twitch and suddenness for his size. He has acceleration and enough top-end to run away from defenders. He also can contribute as a pass-catcher which he showed on the one touchdown reception. He’s had a big year with several of these types of games. Michigan Tech commit Grayson Fellows was very good in leading he win at quarterback. He was efficient, made good decisions, used his feet when he had to, and gave tremendous second effort on a touchdown run that looked dead, but he continued to push and got in. He’s accurate, he throws with good touch down the field and dropped in a beautiful one during this game. He also shows very good timing. He connected with Central Michigan commit Will Fussman on an out that was thrown well before the break and was on the money. Fussman has had a great season. He’s 6’2 with deeper speed and ball skills. He only had a couple targets in this one, but his presence opened up opportunities for Kenowa’s other skill guys to have one on one matchups. Sophomore Kiumani Broussard is the one we are watching closely. He nearly broke a punt return and has some real quickness and explosiveness when he touches the ball. With some very good older skill guys here, he only gets so many opportunities, but he’s a guy who could break out next fall. Christian’s top prospect is Indiana commit Caleb Pugh . He’s been out most of the season with injury, so was just coming back and getting into the swing of the season. He plays guard at Christian but the plan is center at Indiana. This was a camp find by Indiana that could pay off. Pugh is a hard-working lineman who play with good pad level and bend. Hope College quarterback commit Charlie King was very elusive and made a lot of plays with his feet. He got out of several situations where it looked like Kenowa had him tackled. He also hit on a downfield touchdown to senior receiver Brieon Walton , a 6-foot-3 prospect who has a couple of D3 offers.

item.title: WWE Women’s Division Legend Rules Out In-Ring Return Despite Fan Demand
item.description: WWE A WWE Women’s division legend has shut down the possibility of an in-ring return for WWE or any company. She is none other than WWE legend Melina, who was one of the pioneers of women’s wrestling in WWE in the late 2000s. When asked about returning to the ring, her reason for declining made perfect sense. Multi-time champion Melina held a Q&A session on TikTok, and a fan asked about returning to the ring. The former five-time Women’s Champion said that while she loves to watch wrestling and be around it, she does not have the hunger to get back in the ring. Melina noted that wrestling on television was spectacular because today’s in-ring competitors have that hunger. Therefore, she did not want to return half-heartedly and disappoint her fans. “Everyone keeps asking me this and I say no, no. I love to watch, I love to … just be around it. Now, I think those days is just different. I don’t have the hunger and you need the hunger. You need that because you see it. So, when you watch your favorite wrestlers wrestling, if they don’t, they have that hunger. That’s what makes it even better to watch. So, I don’t have that. So, I disappoint you guys and I don’t wanna do that.” WWE Legend, Melina explains why she will never step back into the ring: “I don’t have the hunger and you need that hunger” pic.twitter.com/aUlifOSrwW — FADE (@FadeAwayMedia) October 30, 2026 Melina debuted in WWE in the early 2000s. She was the manager of the MnM tag team (Johnny Nitro and Joey Mercury) and then transitioned into a singles performer. Melina attained incredible success, winning both the WWE Women’s and Divas titles and competing against top stars like Beth Phoenix, Mickie James, and more. However, her spectacular run came to an end in 2011 when WWE released her. Following that, Melina competed on the independent circuit for a few years and continues to make non-wrestling appearances. Meanwhile, she made a few WWE appearances, including being the second participant in the 2022 Women’s Royal Rumble match and having a moment with Sasha Banks. item.title: Suspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigation
item.description: Bets predicted exact top-five men’s finishing order Organiser France Football has contacted police A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police. It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award. Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outlet Upside’s investigation . Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
